correctness.rationale: An inner inverse exists exactly when a weak total section of the image extends; the bipartite image-matching lemma constructs an opposite-side section. A three-part explicit map has two adjacent image points with unique preimages distinct in one independent set, proving nonregularity. Complete and edgeless boundaries reduce to regular full transformation monoids. The complete combinatorial proof handles every finite part size, and exhaustive checks give independent corroboration, not proof.

value.rationale: A complete and sharp structural classification of the semigroup regularity property for every finite complete multipartite graph, showing a uniform positive bipartite result and a minimal four-vertex obstruction on introducing a third part with a duplicate vertex. This materially distinguishes total from partial weak graph maps, a distinction already meaningful in primary literature.
